subject: Post-call: CascadiaPay model assurance & version evidence request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cascadiapay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: CascadiaPay model assurance & version evidence request

Hi Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so your team and procurement have a single source of truth.

Call highlights (30 min):
- Main ask: stable transaction categorization for downstream risk scoring (low tolerance for false positives on high-value transactions).
- Current concern: your QA team reported a spike in misclassifications after a recent hosted-model update (automated rollout on Oct 14).
- Our recommendation: short-term pin to the last-known-good model while we run a focused regression investigation and provide an evidence pack.

What I’m attaching / linking:
- cascadiapay_benchmarks_v1.csv — our initial benchmark set pulled from the sample you shared (rows annotated).
- cascadiapay_promptset_v1.jsonl — the prompt/ground-truth pairs we used in the run.
- Drive folder (linked below) with raw outputs, diff tooling, and the evaluation notebook.

Recommended immediate actions (proposed timeline):
1) You share 30–100 representative failing queries (we’ll accept a redacted CSV). This lets us reproduce locally. (You mentioned procurement/legal concerns about data — scoping the sample is fine.)
2) We pin to the prior model snapshot for production traffic while we investigate (48–96 hour guardrail depending on QA cadence). Pin is reversible.
3) Redwood runs a prioritized regression diff: automated metrics + small manual review on edge cases, and then we deliver an evidence package + suggested guardrails (canary thresholds, token limits).

Open questions from our side:
- Can your team share the timeframe when the spike began and any change in prompt pre-processing?
- Do you want the canary routed by traffic percentage or by HT/merchant whitelist?

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min technical sync Thursday (Oct 22) at 10am PT to review the diff results and agree pin window? I’ll put a tentative invite on the calendar.

Thanks — I’ve cc’d Marcus and Rishi from our platform team for the technical follow-through.

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cascadiapay_benchmarks_v1.csv, cascadiapay_promptset_v1.jsonl

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: CascadiaPay model assurance & version evidence request

Kimberly — appreciate the quick recap and the artifacts. I pulled a short set of failing items into a zip (cascadiapay_sample_fails.zip) and uploaded to the shared drive. Two quick things from our side:

1) Procurement flagged that any pin or SLA change needs a formal scope (we can do a short addendum or memo).
2) We’re OK with a temporary pin but need signal on how long this will impact latency/cost; our ops team is sensitive to any configuration that increases token usage.

I’ve cc'd procurement so we can parallelize the paperwork. I also confirmed the spike starts around Oct 14, consistent with your note. We do not believe there was prompt-engineering change on our side — the integration layer is immutable for that flow.

Tentative for Thu 10am PT is good. If you can send a short agenda (diff scope, canary strategy, pin duration), I’ll bring our lead engineer.

—
Tom Reynolds
Head of Product, CascadiaPay
Tom.Reynolds@cascadiapay.com | +1 (206) 555-0899

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: CascadiaPay model assurance & version evidence request

Kimberly / Rishi — quick internal note before Thursday’s call. I pulled a small smoke diff between the two snapshots (hosted: redwood-13b-v20261014 -> prior: redwood-13b-v20260901). Preliminary observations:
- Token-level generation distributions are within expected variance for ~85% of the sample.
- Failure modes cluster around merchant category edge cases and literal numeric parsing (dates/amounts).
- A small behavior change in the sampling temperature/default top_p was rolled during the Oct 14 deploy (this could explain some divergence).

Recommend immediate tactical steps for Thursday:
- Draft a 1-page diff summary (I attached diff-summary-20261021.txt) that shows sample pairs and metric deltas (precision/recall on flagged classes).
- Propose pin to redwood-13b-v20260901 for production traffic until we ship a fix. Pin implementation: 2–4 hrs to stage, toggle via routing policy, no infra maintenance window required.
- Canary approach: route 5% of traffic to pinned image and 95% to current for 2h, check regressions, then flip 100% if green.

I’ll prepare the diff artifact and the metric table for the call. We should also prepare a short note for procurement (impact/rollback guarantees).

—
Marcus Lin
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: diff-summary-20261021.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cascadiapay.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: CascadiaPay model assurance & version evidence request

Tom / Kimberly / Marcus — adding technical plan and acceptance criteria ahead of Thu’s sync so the call is decision-focused.

Plan (high level):
- Short-term: Pin production route to redwood-13b-v20260901 (model-id: rw-13b-20260901-abc123). This is a configuration change in the routing layer — low risk and reversible. Expected turnaround: 2–4 hours from approval.
- Medium-term: Run prioritized regression suite (your 100 labeled samples + our golden set) and produce an evidence pack (metrics, top 25 diffs, recommended prompt sanitizers). Target: deliver within 48 hours of pin.
- Guardrails / rollback criteria:
  * If false positive rate on high-value transactions increases by >1.5x vs baseline -> automatic rollback trigger.
  * If latency p50 increases by >30ms under typical load -> investigate but do not rollback immediately (unless customer requests).

Operational notes:
- Canary will be implemented via sampling in the routing policy. We suggest 5% -> 25% -> 100% over a 2–6 hour window, with automated checks at each step.
- I opened SUP-12458 to track the config change and audit log (link below). We’ll attach the evidence pack to the ticket.

Tom — if this approach is acceptable, we’ll schedule the pin right after the call and notify your ops channel. We’ll keep a live channel (Slack or WebEx) during the flip.

Rishi
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks team — quick summary of decisions from this morning’s sync and explicit next steps so procurement can track scope: 

Decisions: 
- Redwood will pin production to rw-13b-20260901-abc123 immediately after this thread (targeting today 11:00am PT unless procurement requests delay).
- Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4 hours with automated checks at each step.
- Redwood to deliver evidence pack (metrics, top diffs, prompt set suggestions) within 48 hours of pin.

Actions & owners: 
- Kimberly: send a 1-pager summary for procurement and include estimated cost impact (expected minimal; Marcus to provide worst-case token delta).
- Marcus: finalize diff-summary and the metric table (ETA: 4 hours).
- Rishi: perform the pin and monitor the canary; create SUP-12458 artifact with audit logs.
- Tom / CascadiaPay: provide the redacted sample set (you uploaded cascadiapay_sample_fails.zip) and confirm PO path if procurement will require an addendum.

Procurement note: Redwood confirms the pin is a configuration change only — no new infra. If you require a formal addendum, Kimberly will loop legal; otherwise we will treat this as a short-term operational measure covered under existing terms.

I’ll send the procurement-facing summary now and schedule a brief 15-min follow-up post-canary to confirm the metrics. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

—
